sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a skull measuring 20.0 cm long and 13.0 cm wide, along with a thigh bone 14.2 cm in length.
Its teeth were heterodont, meaning they varied in shape, with large crushing teeth positioned at the rear of the jaws.
The species name honors James Ross McCabe, the man who discovered and prepared the fossil.
Scientists first described the genus Stangerochampsa in 1996.
The fossil was found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta.
Stangerochampsa is classified within the unranked family Globidonta.
However, recent studies have yielded conflicting placements, with the animal recovered as a stem-group caiman in 2021 and as a basal alligatorine in 2022.
This animal lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Brochu (1999) suggested that Stangerochampsa and Albertochampsa were synonymous and placed the genus just outside the family Alligatoridae.
Later, Brochu (2004) and Hill and Lucas (2006) found Stangerochampsa outside of Alligatorinae, with Hill and Lucas identifying Albertochampsa as its sister taxon.
